mainTopic: Gaps and erasures in a שטר, and how the court guards against forgery
overview: The גמרא first raises a problem for רב. According to רב טביומי, רב allows both a filled-in gap between the עדים and the אשרתא and a שטר written over a מחק, and together these seem to open the door to forgery. The answer is that in such a case the court ignores the old אשרתא and confirms the שטר only through its עדים. Then רבי יוחנן rules that a gap of even one line between the עדים and the אשרתא makes the שטר invalid. The reason is that a forger could cut off the top and write a whole one-line document with its witnesses in that gap, and רבי יוחנן holds such a document is valid. The גמרא asks why the same trick doesn't work in a one-line gap above the עדים. It answers that a text on one line with its עדים on the next line is invalid. If the forger writes fake witnesses on his own line, the court checks only those top witnesses, so the forgery fails. Finally the גמרא returns to examine רב's ruling that a שטר written with its עדים over a מחק is valid.

steps.title: A problem for רב according to רב טביומי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no problem if the ruling about a שטר written over a מחק was said by שמואל. But רב טביומי says רב said it, and then רב's two rulings together seem to allow forgery.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for רב כהנא, who teaches it in the name of שמואל. But for רב טביומי, who teaches it in the name of רב, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is raising a difficulty. It depends on who said the ruling that a שטר written over a מחק is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows a filled-in gap between the עדים and the אשרתא. If רב also holds that a שטר and its עדים may be written over a מחק, someone could erase the filled-in gap and write a fake document with signatures there, under a real אשרתא. If the מחק ruling belongs to שמואל, the two rulings come from different people and there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? A formula that raises a difficulty

steps.confusionAlert: The argument between רב כהנא and רב טביומי is not about the law itself. It is only about WHO said it, שמואל or רב. That matters because it decides whether רב holds both rulings at once.

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rav Kahana
phrases.notes: The 'it' here is the earlier ruling that a document and its witnesses written over an erasure are valid.

phrases.english: who teaches it in the name of Shmuel; that is fine.
But according to Rav Tavyumei
who teaches it in the name of Rav,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא אֶלָּא לְרַב טָבְיוֹמֵי מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines two earlier rulings on the daf and points out a forgery risk if רב said both.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling allowing a filled-in gap between the עדים and the אשרתא, according to רב טביומי's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a שטר written over a מחק is valid, someone could erase the filled-in gap and write a forged document there, and it would appear backed by the real אשרתא.

steps.title: The court relies on the witnesses, not the old ratification
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that in such a case the court does not rely on the אשרתא at all. It confirms the שטר only through its עדים, so the forgery would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: in every case like this, we do not confirm the document from the אשרתא on it, only from the עדים on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty for רב. When a שטר is written over a מחק, the old אשרתא counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear was that a forged text would "borrow" a real court's אשרתא. If the court ignores the אשרתא whenever the document sits on a מחק, and checks only the עדים, the forger gains nothing. The real witnesses will not confirm a document they never signed.

keyTerms.meaning: A court's ratification written on a document

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, when a שטר is written over a מחק, the old אשרתא is ignored. Only the עדים themselves can confirm it, so the forgery fear goes away.

phrases.english: He holds: in every case like this,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב. 'A case like this' means a document written over an erasure that has a court ratification on it.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְקַיְּימִין אוֹתוֹ מִן הָאַשַּׁרְתָּא שֶׁבּוֹ,
phrases.english: we do not confirm it from the ratification on it,
but only from the witnesses on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a limiting rule about how such a document is confirmed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the old אשרתא would make a forged text over the מחק look valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: In such cases the אשרתא is ignored, and only the עדים can confirm the document, so no forgery is possible.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a gap before the court's ratification invalidates
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the rule that a one-line gap is allowed. It applies only between the text and the עדים. Between the עדים and the אשרתא, even one line makes the שטר invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They taught this only about a gap between the עדים and the text. But between the עדים and the אשרתא, even one line makes it invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is brought. רבי יוחנן says the leniency about a one-line gap does not cover the space above the court's אשרתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed a gap of up to one line between the text and the signatures. רבי יוחנן says that allowance applies only there. A blank line between the עדים and the אשרתא is treated more strictly, and even one line disqualifies the document.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only (in the case of...): a limiting formula
The written text of the document

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּין הָעֵדִים לַכְּתָב,
phrases.english: They taught this only about a gap between the witnesses and the text,
but between the witnesses and the ratification,
even one line makes it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּין הָעֵדִים לַכְּתָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different view on gaps between the עדים and the אשרתא, stricter than the approach discussed for רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of even one line between the עדים and the אשרתא invalidates the שטר. The one-line allowance applies only between the text and the עדים.

steps.title: Why is the gap before the ratification different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא should be stricter than a gap between the text and the עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's strictness. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are blank spaces of one line, so it is not obvious why one is allowed and the other is not. The גמרא wants to know what forgery risk exists only above the אשרתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason for a distinction

phrases.english: What is different about a gap between the witnesses and the ratification?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What forgery danger makes a one-line gap above the אשרתא invalid, when the same gap above the עדים is allowed?

steps.title: The fear: cut off the top and write a one-line document
steps.stepSummary: Someone could cut off the original document at the top and write a new, one-line document with its witnesses inside the gap. The real אשרתא below would then seem to approve it. רבי יוחנן holds that such a one-line document is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will cut off the top and write the document and its witnesses on one line. And רבי יוחנן holds that a שטר that comes with its text and witnesses on one line is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the danger behind רבי יוחנן's rule. The next step challenges this reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is one blank line above the אשרתא, a forger could remove everything above it and fit a complete short document, text and signatures together, into that line. Since רבי יוחנן holds a one-line document is valid, the forgery would succeed and appear backed by the court. That is why even one line in that spot disqualifies the שטר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's strictness comes from two ideas together: a blank line above the אשרתא is room for a whole new document, and he holds that a one-line document with its עדים is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason depends on רבי יוחנן's own view that a one-line שטר is valid. Steps 6 through 9 test whether the same danger should also apply to a gap between the text and the עדים.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will cut off the upper part,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person holding the document. 'The upper part' is the original text and signatures.

phrases.english: and write the document and its witnesses on one line,
and he holds: a document that comes with its text and its witnesses
on one line is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא גָּיֵיז לְעִילַּאי, וְכָתֵב הוּא וְעֵדָיו בְּשִׁיטָה אַחַת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A forger could cut off the top and write a complete one-line document with its witnesses in the gap above the אשרתא. Since רבי יוחנן holds such a document is valid, the gap must be forbidden.

steps.title: The same forgery should work in the gap above the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: If a one-line gap above the אשרתא is dangerous, a one-line gap between the text and the עדים should be just as dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same worry should apply to a gap between the עדים and the text. Maybe he will cut off the top, write whatever he wants in the empty line, and the real עדים are already signed below it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reason from Step 5 and turns it against רבי יוחנן's own leniency, which allows a one-line gap between the text and the עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the danger was that a forger could cut off the real document and write a new one-line שטר in the empty space. The same trick seems to work above the עדים: cut off the text, write a new line, and the real signatures below seem to confirm it. So why is that gap allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is right

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, בֵּין עֵדִים לַכְּתָב נָמֵי –
phrases.english: If so, between the witnesses and the text as well:
perhaps he will cut off the top part,
and write whatever he wants,
and the witnesses are already signed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בֵּין עֵדִים לַכְּתָב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of Step 5 to challenge the leniency in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's allowance of a one-line gap between the text and the עדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forgery danger that makes the gap above the אשרתא forbidden seems to apply equally to the gap above the עדים.

steps.title: A one-line document with witnesses on the next line is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that a שטר with its text on one line and its עדים on the following line is פסול, so the forger gains nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: a שטר that comes with its text on one line and its עדים on a different line is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the forger's new one-line שטר would be invalid anyway, because its עדים would be signed on the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the gap above the אשרתא, the forger can fit both a text and its עדים into the one empty line, and רבי יוחנן holds such a שטר is valid. Above the עדים, the forger can only write a text line, and the real signatures sit on the line below it. A one-line שטר signed like that is פסול, so the forgery fails.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his view

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: שְׁטָר הַבָּא הוּא בְּשִׁיטָה אַחַת,
phrases.english: He holds: a document that comes with its text on one line,
and its witnesses on another line, is invalid.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the feared forgery would produce an invalid document.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forged one-line text above the real עדים would be accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: A one-line text with its עדים on the next line is פסול, so the trick does not work.

steps.title: What if he writes the text and fake witnesses on the same line?
steps.stepSummary: The forger could write the text and his own עדים together on the one line, then claim the real signatures below are extra witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us worry that he will write the text and its עדים on one line, and say: I added the extra עדים below to have more witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. The forger can avoid the 'next line' problem by fitting the text and fake signatures together in the one empty line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the one-line שטר is valid in form, because its עדים are on the same line as the text. The real signatures left underneath are explained away as extra עדים added to make the matter more public. So the gap above the עדים looks dangerous again.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא כָּתֵב הוּא וְעֵדָיו בְּשִׁיטָה אַחַת,
phrases.english: And let us worry that perhaps he will write it and its witnesses on one line,
phrases.notes: He writes this in the empty line after cutting away the real text above it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: אֲנָא לְרַבּוֹת בְּעֵדִים הוּא דַּעֲבַדִי!
phrases.english: and say: I did it to add more witnesses!
phrases.notes: His excuse for the real signatures that sit below his line.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא כָּתֵב הוּא וְעֵדָיו בְּשִׁיטָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 7 with a smarter forgery.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the forged one-line שטר would be invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fake עדים are on the same line as the text, the שטר is valid in form, and the real signatures below just look like extra witnesses.

steps.title: The court confirms such a document only through the top witnesses
steps.stepSummary: In such a case the court confirms the שטר only through the עדים on the line of the text, not through the ones below, so the fake signatures would be exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: in any case like this, we do not confirm the שטר through the עדים below, only through the עדים above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the court ignores the lower signatures and checks only the עדים written on the same line as the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forger's own fake signatures are the top עדים, and they cannot be confirmed as real. The real signatures below give him no help, so the forgery fails. Over a gap above the אשרתא, the real אשרתא would confirm the fake line, which is why only that gap is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: "The witnesses above" are not the original signers. They are the ones written on the same line as the text, which in the forgery case are the forger's fake witnesses.
steps.whatToRemember: A one-line gap above the עדים is allowed because every forgery there fails. A one-line gap above the אשרתא is פסול because there the real אשרתא would seem to approve a forged line.

phrases.english: He holds: in any case like this,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְקַיְּימִין אוֹתוֹ מִן הָעֵדִים שֶׁלְּמַטָּה,
phrases.english: we do not confirm it through the witnesses below,
but only through the witnesses above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 and closes this line of questioning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the court would confirm such a שטר, which blocks the forgery.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The real signatures below would back up the forged line.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the top עדים count for confirming the שטר, and the forger's fake ones would be exposed.

steps.title: Back to רב's ruling about a document written over an erasure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to look at רב's statement itself: a שטר whose text and עדים are both written over a מחק is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב said: a שטר that comes with its text and its עדים written over an erasure is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's ruling, which came up earlier, to discuss it on its own. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling was quoted back in Step 1 as part of a challenge. The word גּוּפָא shows that the גמרא now studies that ruling directly. The point is that when both the text and the signatures are on a מחק, the שטר is still כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; going back to a statement quoted earlier
An erased spot on the writing surface

phrases.english: The matter itself. רב said:
phrases.notes: This is the ruling of רב that came up in Step 1.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטָר הַבָּא הוּא וְעֵדָיו עַל הַמְּחָק – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: A document that comes with it and its witnesses on an erasure is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יוחנן's gap discussion and returns to the ruling of רב first mentioned in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שטר whose text and עדים are both written over a מחק is כשר.
